2607.04962.title: Who's Behind It? Annotating and Extracting Conspiratorial Actors from German Telegram Posts
2607.04962.paper_summary: Conspiracy theories commonly attribute important events to the actions of powerful and secretive actors. While computational research has largely focused on document-level analyses of conspiracy theories, less attention has been paid to identifying the actors that drive such narratives. We develop annotation guidelines for conspiratorial actors, present a span-annotated corpus of German Telegram posts, and investigate their automatic extraction using transformer-based models. We further apply the resulting model to the \textit{Schwurbelarchiv}, a large-scale archive of German conspiracy-related Telegram channels. Our results demonstrate that conspiratorial actors can be annotated with meaningful agreement and extracted with reasonable accuracy despite the linguistic complexity of conspiracy discourse, enabling large-scale analyses of actor representations in conspiracy narratives.
2607.04962.paper_summary_zh: 陰謀論通常將重要事件歸因於強大且神秘的行動者。<lb/>雖然計算研究主要集中在陰謀論的文件級分析上，但對於識別推動這些敘事的行動者的關注卻較少。<lb/>我們制定了針對陰謀行動者的標註指南，呈現了一個德國Telegram帖子範圍標註的語料庫，並調查了使用基於Transformer的模型進行自動提取的可能性。<lb/>我們進一步將所得到的模型應用於\textit{Schwurbelarchiv}，這是一個大型德國陰謀相關Telegram頻道的檔案庫。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，陰謀行動者可以以有意義的協議進行標註，並且儘管陰謀話語的語言複雜性，仍能以合理的準確性進行提取，從而使對陰謀敘事中行動者表現的大規模分析成為可能。
